_readme: LoreRim Glue - status rules and thresholds. Do NOT edit this file: copy it to lrg_config.json (same folder) and edit the copy; your copy overrides these defaults key by key and survives plugin updates. Faction / class patterns are matched against EditorIDs with * wildcards, case-insensitive, so factions added by LoreRim's mods can be covered without any FormIDs.

affinity._readme: Affinity comes from CHIM's relationship_system (-100..100). Vanilla relationship rank (-4..4) is read as an input only and is never written. [0.3.1] trust_our_last_known: CHIM deletes an NPC's relationship entry on almost every save reload (NpcMaster::restoreNPC rewrites extended_data.relationships from a history row, and a row without the key strips it), which is why an NPC you have been with can read 'not close enough' after a load. The glue keeps its own copy in lrg_romance.last_affinity and uses it when CHIM's entry is missing, or when CHIM says 0 and we remember better. Every rescue is logged. log_rescue=false silences that line only.

relationship._readme: [0.3.1 / R1b] A scene that really happened raises her affinity towards the player a little, through CHIM's own RelationshipManager::adjustRelationship (entry created if absent, clamped to -100..100, the relationship TYPE never touched - CHIM reserves the romantic ones). Guards: the scene must have run min_scene_seconds and ended normally or by 'stop' (a crash, a reload or a lost thread gives nothing), and at most one gain per NPC per gain_window_seconds of real time. The SAME two guards decide whether lrg_romance.scenes is counted up at all (lrgSceneCounted), so a cancelled start can no longer pay the history bonus. min_scene_seconds (60) is deliberately HIGHER than outro.min_scene_seconds (45): a short scene still earns a proper goodbye, it just does not move the relationship. An NPC whose relationships are locked in CHIM's NPC manager is never written to (CHIM's own setters do not honour that flag, so the glue checks it itself).
relationship._gain_window_readme: [0.3.1 fix pass] Was 21600 (6 real hours), which meant a whole evening together was worth one gain and the owner's 'sex should slightly improve the relationship' would hardly be felt. 1800 = half a real hour: two separate times together in one evening are worth two gains, while a scene restarted right after a stop still counts once. Raise it again if affinity climbs too fast.
relationship._repair_readme: [0.3.1 / R1d] A ONE-TIME, idempotent repair of an affinity CHIM's restoreNPC destroyed. It runs inside the first live game turn with that NPC after the deploy (never from the CLI: the write has to carry the game timestamp or the next reload rolls it back), writes through RelationshipManager::setRelationship with no type, logs exactly what it did, and marks itself done in lrg_memory so it can never run twice. SET enabled=false ONCE IT HAS RUN (look for 'relationship repair: <npc> -> Player set to <n>' in lorerim_glue.log). NOTE for the owner: 18 was CHIM's last good value for Lisette (written 17:19:58 on 2026-09-21, history row 279) - the 10 the glue used to log was the courting bonus and was never CHIM's number. THE NUMBER: 26 = that 18 plus the ONE scene gain the shipped rule would really have granted on 2026-09-21 (+8 for the first scene; the second scene was three minutes later and is inside any gain window). The 30 that was shipped assumed two gains that day and is 4 higher than the code's own arithmetic; if the owner prefers the round 30, that is her call, but it is a deliberate round-up, not the rule. [pt15] SHIPPED DISABLED: the Lisette repair ran once on the owner's own game (its marker is in that game's lrg_memory). The marker is per database, so on a FRESH install (or after lrg_memory is wiped) an enabled block would fire again and overwrite a real, newer relationship with 26. The block stays here, documented, as the template for a future one-off repair: set enabled=true, name the NPC and the affinity, deploy, play one turn with her, then set it back to false.

repair.why: playtest 7: CHIM's own restoreNPC wiped the entry on four reloads; 18 was the last good value, plus the first-scene gain of that day

outro._readme: [0.3.1 / R3] When a scene ends the game asks for one more turn (request type lrg_scenetalk, text 'outro'). The server answers it with a dedicated goodbye directive: two to four plain sentences about what they actually did, what the player is to her now, and what she does next and why - taken from what CHIM knows about her life. It is the one turn around a scene that is NOT capped at one sentence. window_seconds is how long the ticket written at the scene end stays valid; min_scene_seconds keeps a cancelled start quiet. The ticket is consumed after one use, so an outro can never fire twice. NOTE: this min_scene_seconds (45, and the game's own fOutroMinScene) is deliberately LOWER than relationship.min_scene_seconds (60) - a 45-59 second scene gets a proper goodbye and no affinity gain. That asymmetry is intended, not a bug.

leverage._readme: External pull on a decision. Passed to the LLM as words, never as numbers. Gold only ever moves when the NPC accepts an offer in conversation. [0.3.1 / R1c] history_bonus: what their own history is worth on the INTEREST score (kept separate from affinity so the two stay readable in one log line, and so a history bonus can never be written back into CHIM's store). base once they have been together at all, + history_bonus_per_extra for every further scene, capped at history_bonus_max. It is what stops an NPC you have already been with from reading 'not close enough' again after a reload.

renown.dragonborn_known: is known across Skyrim as the Dragonborn
renown.many_deeds: has a growing reputation for deeds across the holds
renown.unknown: is nobody in particular to them

privacy_defaults._door_readme: [0.4] A CLOSED DOOR MAKES A ROOM PRIVATE. Until 0.4 the game counted every awake adult within the hearing radius as a witness with no line-of-sight test at all - through a closed door, a floor or a stone wall - so a room in a busy inn could never reach zero witnesses whatever door was shut. From 0.4 the game reports door=1 when the player is in an interior and every door within fDoorRadius is closed, and then an NPC who can see NEITHER of you no longer counts just for being near. SEEN IS STILL SEEN: Actor.HasLOS ignores the door state, so an open doorway, a shared room and a balcony above still count, door or no door. These two numbers are unchanged and still decide the rest: max_witnesses is how many onlookers a profile tolerates (0 for everyone by default) and followers_ok whether the player's own companions count. The radius and the door distance are MCM sliders (fHearRadius 600, fDoorRadius 250); bPrivacyDoors switches the whole door rule off and restores the old behaviour.

_followers_readme: [0.5.1] OWNER ADDENDUM 10 - CHIM AND THE FOLLOWER MODS. The framework in this modlist is Simple Follower Framework, NOT Nether's Follower Framework: CHIM's own MakeFollower ends in a dead 'if (nwsFF)' branch here and leaves the NPC half-recruited - in the vanilla CurrentFollowerFaction with no teammate flag, no framework alias and no slot accounting. That state (the game reports it as ghost:1 inside the snapshot's fol= block) is why 'it's time for us to part ways' spoken to her dismisses the player's REAL follower instead: SFF resolves the target of a follower command by alias membership and falls through to the primary follower for an actor that is in none. The game repairs it (MCM: Followers), and the three switches below are the server's half. hide_when_cap_full reads SFF's own SFF_CanRecruitMore global off the snapshot, so 'join my party' disappears when the follower framework says no slot is free. That is NOT the same test as the vanilla recruit entry, which is conditioned on PlayerFollowerCount == 0 and which SFF blocks as soon as it has any follower at all: SFF_CanRecruitMore is the looser of the two, so this rule only ever hides an action that genuinely cannot work. block emits <companion_status>, which is facts only and never duplicates CHIM's own <adventuring_party>. warn_actions only WRITES A LINE IN THE LOG - switching a CHIM action off is the owner's call, in the CHIM web UI.

followers._remember_readme: [0.5.4 / pt13] Game script 504/505 retires the whole fol= block for the rest of a session whenever its snapshot abort rail THINKS a snapshot died in it (playtest 13: six false alarms). The server keeps the last fol= the SAME session (snapshot sess tag) sent for this long, so the companion block, the hide rule and the escort's 'never for a framework's follower' rail do not go quiet for the session. 0 = forget at once (the 0.5.3 behaviour). A snapshot without a sess tag never remembers anything.

_escort_readme: [0.5.4 / pt13] FOLLOW / WAIT / RELEASE - 'I couldn't get her to follow me'. CHIM chose Follow_<player> three times and its package really went on, but Lisette was back in a running ENGINE scene (the bard's stage) and a scene outranks every package. recognise: 'follow me', 'come with me (somewhere private / upstairs / to my room)', 'come along', a bare 'come on', 'walk with me', 'wait here', 'stay here', 'you can go (back)' are read as a request in EVERY mode outside a scene with her (questions, negations, hypotheticals stay nothing). directive: follow -> choose Follow_<player> (or her real follower entry when the menuless follower kind is live) and answer in one short line; wait / release -> CHIM's WaitHere is switched off in the catalog, so nothing is chosen and the glue carries them. emit: the post-LLM gate appends ExtCmdLRG_Escort@ok=1;cid;npc;do=follow|wait|release;safe=<safe_quests> - follow only when she is in an engine scene (snapshot scene=1 / gate reason quest_scene) and the reply carries FollowPlayer or no movement at all; wait / release on the player's own words. Never for a companion a follower framework or the player's party owns (fol= fw sff/custom, mate, ghost, or follower_factions on fac= when no fol= is known): her own dialogue does that. safe_quests: quest EditorID patterns (* and ?) whose running scene the GAME may stop so she can walk away; anything else is left alone and the game answers with a reason. phrases: your own extra player phrases, whole words.

escort._sff_readme: [pt17 / script 509] THE HAND-OFF TO SIMPLE FOLLOWER FRAMEWORK (owner: 'lets change it to whatever follower mod is managing it and work with it that way'). sff_owned: a companion SFF owns (fol= fw:sff) and CHIM's half-recruited ghost are the GAME's to route now - do=follow / wait / release go out for them (the game makes her follow again / wait through SFF's own calls, or recruits the ghost properly); fw:custom, mate:1 without SFF and follower_factions on fac= are still skipped (her own dialogue), and the directive then tells her to SAY so instead of agreeing to nothing. sff_promote: OUTSIDE an engine scene a 'follow me' the player asked for (conf=high) goes out as do=follow when the game can hand her to SFF right now (fol= says fw none/chim, mate 0, pff >= 0, cap 1) - the reply carrying Follow_<player> or no movement at all, as in a scene; the game recruits her (or comes back with fb=<reason> and the old CHIM follow). When the escort carries a follow the framework may take, CHIM's own Follow_<player> line is dropped from the batch (its priority-100 override would sit on the new companion; the game re-adds CHIM's follow itself in the fallback). voice_fallback: an OK funcret that came with fb= ('comes along, but not as his sworn companion') is voiced in CHIM's funcret turn like a failure; when the voice gap skips it, her next turn is told through the missed note. false = the note only.

words.release: to let you go back to what you were doing

_quiet_readme: [pt19 / script 511] QUIET MODE - Helgen 2026-09-24: the keep intro never reached MQ101 stage 240 and the log could not show what the glue did on Hadvar / Ralof. The GAME decides (LRG_Main.QuietOn: a curated scripted quest - MQ101 from stage 5, QUIET_QUESTS in LRG_Main.psc, MCM bQuietIntro - is running) and says so as quiet=1 on the facts line (ev=facts) and the snapshot. While that is fresh for an NPC, CHIM's own movement / re-tasking actions (lib/lrg_actions.php LRG_MOVEMENT_ACTIONS, plus hide) are withheld from the offer - an OFFER change, never a mute: she answers in words and line rides prompt_bottom so the refusal has its reason (NEVER SILENT). enabled: the whole server half. fresh_seconds: how old the last quiet=1 may be. hide: codes withheld in addition to LRG_MOVEMENT_ACTIONS. names: quest EditorID -> the words <quest> becomes in line. Log: 'quiet: withheld ...' once per NPC per spell, 'quiet: released ...' after it.

quiet.line: <npc> is inside a scripted scene of the game (<quest>) - <npc> cannot be led, followed, sent away or dismissed until it is over, and says so plainly if asked.

_voice_readme: [0.5.5 / owner addendum 11] NEVER SILENT - 'if she's busy she should say that then and it will be fine'. enabled: a glue command that FAILS (escort refused, clothes that would not come off, an unreachable position, a start the game refused ...) is answered in the same exchange: CHIM runs its own funcret follow-up turn and she says, in one short line, what did not happen and why (every glue row has the follow-up on since actions v11; the glue ends every result that must stay silent - a success, the kill switch - before the MAIN lock). lead_failures: her own move on a scene-lead tick is told on her next turn instead (false). min_gap_seconds: at most one voiced turn per NPC in this many seconds. max_tokens: the cap of that one line. watch: CHIM's own ComeCloser / MoveTo / TravelTo / FollowPlayer (when no escort went out) are judged by the next snapshots - still in an engine scene, or not closer to the player after min_seconds - and her next player turn is told she did not manage it; no evidence within max_seconds = nothing is said.

voice._dry_run_readme: [pt17] dry_run_voiced: a refusal caused by the LoreRim Glue DEVELOPER dry run (MCM > Diagnostics > 'DEV: dry-run everything') is voiced like any other failure - she says plainly that the switch is on and where it is, the one time the game's own settings may be named. Playtest 2026-09-23: seven correct requests were refused in silence because the old code kept a dry run quiet on purpose ('a dry run changes nothing'). false restores that silence (told on her next turn instead).

_never_empty_readme: [pt17-replies / owner addendum 11] NEVER EMPTY (lib/lrg_replies.php). Captain Aldis, 2026-09-23 20:10:31: the model answered a schema-valid JSON whose message was empty and nothing was spoken - 17 of 322 logged replies (5.3 %) since the log began look like that. enabled: a reply with no words on a player-speech / lrg_dlgtalk / voiced-funcret turn is caught. reask: one more LLM call with the rule 'answer in words' appended before any floor line (about 1.5-2 s on the few turns it happens; false = the floor line straight away, and an action-bearing empty reply keeps its action). in_scene: also inside an OStim scene / the outro (default off: log only there). note_seconds: how long the next-turn rule ('her last reply carried no words ...') rides the prompt. lines: the SPOKEN floor lines, rotated per NPC - question (the player asked something), statement (he did not), trouble (no reply at all / invalid output: she did not catch it - never a line that implies she heard and understood). max_chars caps each. grep lorerim_glue.log for 'never-empty' to count how often the model does it.

question: Hm. Ask me that again.
I'm not sure what to tell you.
Give me a moment to think on that.

_never_false_readme: [pt18-words / PROTOCOL 10.22, 10.25] NEVER FALSE (lib/lrg_replies.php, the section at the end). General Tullius, 2026-09-23 23:19: 'i swear to uphold the imperial vows' got 'Then you are a Legionnaire. Report to Legate Rikke at the training yard for your first orders.' while the game's own facts line said CW00A stage 0 before and after - nothing was recorded, and the prompt rule ('nothing has begun') had been ignored twice. On a faction turn (this NPC recruits for, or belongs to, a faction row, or an enlistment was asked) every sentence of the reply is judged, in the chunk that completed it: a claimed rank or membership (member), an oath administered here and now (oath), the recruiter's next step by name (next: 'report to Legate Rikke' - a guard's redirect is exempt) and an appointment the game never records (orders: training yard, barracks, 'for your first orders', 'at dawn', 'when the bell rings', 'your training begins') are FALSE unless the game's quest stages say otherwise (rows.<id>.truth: quest -> minimum stage, from UESP; the stages come from the facts line qst=, the quest lane's executed flag, a fresher exec_qst, and the row's recruiters' cached facts lines - quest stages are global). A quest absent from every source is UNKNOWN and the claim passes with verdict=unknown (a completed quest never appears in qst=), except where rows.<id>.derive knows better (CW01A cannot have started while CW00A runs below 10). mode: reask (default) = the false sentence stops the stream and she is asked ONCE more with her own sentence quoted as false (about 1.5-2 s), then one truthful floor line if she does it again; a reply carrying a dialogue pick, or whose action is not known yet, is never rejected - the sentence is dropped per sentence and the floor line spoken after the stream (no second call). mute = always the drop + floor line, never a second LLM call (the fallback if a live re-ask ever misbehaves). log = judge and log only. lines: the SPOKEN floor lines by role (recruiter / redirect / none), rotated per NPC, max_chars each; note_seconds: how long the next-turn rule rides the prompt; cache_seconds: how long another NPC's facts line stands in. grep lorerim_glue.log for 'never-false' - every verdict line carries ml= cal= ambient= open=, which is WHY enlistment cannot start by voice at the map table under ml=0.

never_false._price_readme: [pt19-purchase] price: on a turn where the snapshot carries a vendor's stock (or an innkeeper's room price), every price frame she speaks - 'that'll be one septim', 'costs 12 gold', 'for twenty septims' - is judged against the list (the stock prices, the order's total, a live entry, the room, the bounty, the purse); a figure not on it is false: re-asked once with her own sentence quoted and the allowed prices named, then the vendor floor line ({item} / {price} are the list's own), and nothing is sold under it.

recruiter: Nobody is sworn in by a word at this table. Enlistment is done the proper way, or not at all.
I take no oath here. Come to me properly and we will see about your enlistment.
redirect: That is not mine to grant. Enlistment is done properly, by the ones who take recruits.
I cannot sign anyone up. Ask the ones who take recruits, the proper way.
none: I cannot enlist anyone. Nothing has begun.
That is not something I can settle. Nothing has begun.
vendor: I only ask what my list says: {item} is {price} septims.
The price is what it is - {item}, {price} septims, no more and no less.

never_false._rows_readme: Per faction row (the other rows carry ranks only in code, lrgNfDefaults). legion, from https://en.uesp.net/wiki/Skyrim:Joining_the_Legion and https://en.uesp.net/wiki/Skyrim:The_Jagged_Crown_(Imperial): CW00A 10 = spoken directly to General Tullius (he sends the player to Rikke); CW01A 1 = Rikke has set the Fort Hraggstad test, 100 = report back to Rikke, 160 = take the oath, 200 = done (the quest stops running); CW02A 10 = the first assignment of a member. derive: CW01A / CW02A are at 0 while CW00A runs below 10. allow: the fort order is true from CW01A 1. A faction row's own cells of the same name (dialogue.factions.rows.<id>.truth ...) win over these.

CW00A.10: he is sent to Legate Rikke

CW01A.1: Legate Rikke has set him the test at Fort Hraggstad
CW01A.100: he is to report back to Legate Rikke
CW01A.160: he is to take the oath

_paid_intimacy_readme: OWNER ADDENDA 6 - 'EVERYONE HAS A PRICE'. Prices are expressed in DAYS OF WAGE and turned into gold by the server: [pt15 / addenda 12e-f] a day is HER day - band days x the day wage of her own trade (wage_tiers below), so a jarl's day is not a farmhand's. price_multiplier (and the MCM price multiplier) still rescale the whole economy at once. A price is only ever NEEDED when the NPC is not already willing (interest score < 0): a WILLING NPC IS NEVER FOR SALE - she is interested, and money would only insult her. Gold removes exactly ONE gate reason (not_close_enough) and nothing else: never, married-refuse, witnesses, a companion present, a child nearby, combat, a quest scene, adults-only and the kill switch are all untouched, and a refusal she gives for any other reason stands. not_for_sale removes the whole subject: money is then never mentioned to her at all, which is what stops the model inventing a price for somebody who has none. The number the LLM is told is her FLOOR, never a fixed fee - she may name any higher figure in her own voice, and gold can never exceed a number the PLAYER said out loud. Nothing is refunded if the player stops early.

paid_intimacy._ignore_game_switch_readme: THE MISSING-INI-KEY ESCAPE HATCH. bPaidIntimacy is an MCM toggle that defaults ON, but a boolean MCM setting whose default line is not in MCM/Config/LoreRimGlue/settings.ini reads as 0/FALSE - so the game would send paidok=0 and this whole feature would be silently off. Look for 'NOTE these 0.4 settings read OFF' in lorerim_glue.log right after a game load: if bPaidIntimacy is in that list, either add `bPaidIntimacy = 1` under [Intimacy] in settings.ini (the proper fix) or set this key to true, which makes the server ignore the game's switch entirely.
paid_intimacy._wage_readme: [pt15 / OWNER ADDENDA 12e-f] THE WAGE ANCHOR, PER TRADE. Replaces the single gold_per_day_of_wage (35), which is no longer read. The owner's anchor: '3-10 gold per hour average, 20-40 for skilled / special trades, 40 the top end (alchemy, enchanting)'; the court is above all of that. wage_tiers is GOLD PER HOUR and a day is hours_per_day of it: common 5 = 40/day (beggars, tavern folk, commoners, farmers, servants, anyone unknown), performer 8 = 64/day (bards), trade 12.5 = 100/day (merchants, innkeepers, guards, hunters, priests), fighter 16.5 = 132/day (adventurers, mercenaries, housecarls, guard captains), craft_magic 25 = 200/day (smiths, alchemists, enchanters, mages, court wizards, healers), court 62.5 = 500/day (stewards, thanes, nobles, jarls). Which tier an NPC gets, first hit wins: npc_overrides.<name>.wage_tier, then wage_tier_by_job (her real trade inside a broad status rule - each row only refines the rule ids it lists in 'profiles', so it can never move a jarl or a priest), then the matched status rule's own wage_tier (fallback.wage_tier for an unknown faction), then default_wage_tier. An unknown tier name reads as default_wage_tier, never as 0. Her floor = band days (curious) or ceiling days (indifferent) x money_influence x modifiers x her day wage x price_multiplier, rounded to round_to. The price log line shows it as wage=<tier>/<where it came from> gph=<gold per hour> day_wage=<gold>.
paid_intimacy._max_price_readme: [pt15] 2000000, was 200000: with per-trade wages an indifferent jarl is 3000 days x 500 = 1500000, and the old cap would have flattened her to the same figure as a curious one. The cap is a sanity limit only; no shipped profile reaches it.
paid_intimacy._bands_readme: [floor, ceiling] in DAYS OF WAGE, used when the matched status rule carries no price_band of its own. The owner's own ladder: beggars half a day to two days, tavern folk and poor commoners one to four, modest folk and merchants four to fifteen, comfortable folk fifteen to sixty, court and housecarls sixty to three hundred, jarls and nobles three hundred to three thousand ('ridiculous', and that is the point - a jarl is effectively immune unless she wants the player anyway).
paid_intimacy._money_influence_readme: How strongly coin moves this character: a factor ON THE DAYS, so 'insulting' does not mean 'impossible', it means exorbitant - which is the owner's whole point. Derived from the profile's existing gold_sway when the profile sets no money_influence of its own. NOTE for your own lrg_config.json: every shipped status rule carries an EXPLICIT money_influence (it is what makes the recommended price table reproducible), and an explicit value always wins over gold_sway. [pt15 / addenda 12e-f] Every shipped rule and the fallback now carry money_influence 1.0: the owner's calibration is band days x her own day wage and nothing else (Katana, adventurer, curious = 4 days x 132 = 530 after rounding; a modest merchant 400-1500), so the wage tiers and the bands carry the whole difference between a beggar and a jarl. The gold_sway map below only prices a status rule of your own that sets no money_influence, and npc_overrides can still set one for one character (Serana's 4.0). So to change how much coin moves ONE character, set money_influence in npc_overrides.<name> - changing only their gold_sway there moves the prompt words and not the price.
paid_intimacy._stance_readme: Where inside the band she starts, taken from the interest WORD lrgInterest() already produces. Only 'indifferent' and 'curious' ever produce a price at all; 'interested' and 'drawn' are free, because she wants the player (owner: 'genuinely interested -> no price needed'). A free NPC may still ask for a GIFT, capped by token_days.
paid_intimacy._modifier_readme: secret_factor: an NPC married to somebody else under married_rule 'secret' is risking her marriage, so the price triples. repeat_factor: a standing arrangement is a little cheaper. renown_discount mirrors interest.renown_bonus - [unknown, many deeds, Dragonborn] per the profile's renown_sway - so status and fame make her cheaper, which is the 'massive symbols of status and wealth' half of the owner's request.
paid_intimacy._ttl_readme: offer_ttl_seconds has to survive THE WALK: the player offers in the tavern (mode public, reasons=witnesses), she suggests going somewhere private, they walk, and the gate only sees mode private minutes later - playtest 8 took seven minutes over exactly that. Hence 600 and not 180. Both the offer and her own last quote are cleared outright at ev=start and ev=end, so an offer can never be spent twice. quote_ttl_seconds is how long a bare 'deal' can still close a figure she named.
paid_intimacy._confirm_readme: [0.5.6 / pt15, owner ruling C] A GREY offer - an 'if' ('if you ... I'd give you a thousand gold'), a 'would' ('would fifty do?'), or a figure only implied ('a thousand gold for a night') - is never acted on. When it clears her floor and his purse she asks ONE short confirming question and the server remembers the offer (lrg_memory.offer_pending) for confirm_ttl_seconds; his 'yes' / 'deal' / 'done' / 'that's right' / 'I mean it' / the same figure again makes it a FIRM offer at that amount, 'no' / 'forget it' takes it back, a different figure replaces it. Only a FIRM figure at or above her floor that he is actually carrying (pgold) lifts not_close_enough (ruling B: the gold is the trust); a firm figure he is not carrying is called out in her own words (ruling D).
paid_intimacy._gain_readme: paid_gain_factor: paid sex counts half for the relationship gain (owner's wording). It applies whenever gold really moved, including a willing NPC's token gift; set it to 1.0 to switch the penalty off.

status_rules.note: sworn Vigilant of Stendarr; treats any advance as a moral failing and refuses

status_rules._price_note: Everyone has a price and so does a jarl - hers is a fortune nobody could pay (3000 days x 500 = 1500000 septims to somebody she is indifferent to, 300 days x 500 = 150000 if she is at least curious), which is what 'very immune' means here. If she genuinely wants the player, no coin is needed at all. Keys beginning with _ are notes and are NEVER put into a prompt: a figure must never reach the LLM except through the price machinery, or the model would quote it to an NPC who has no price.
status_rules.note: a Jarl: high status, guarded, fears scandal above all; needs deep trust and total privacy

status_rules._price_note: court tier, 500 a day: 30000 curious / 150000 indifferent. A court wizard in this rule is refined to craft_magic (200 a day: 12000 / 60000) by paid_intimacy.wage_tier_by_job.
status_rules.note: court or nobility: reputation is currency; cautious, discreet, slow to trust
a housecarl: duty first; loyalty and respect matter far more than charm

status_rules._price_note: trade tier, 100 a day: 1500 curious / 6000 indifferent. A guard captain is refined to fighter (132 a day: 1980 / 7920) by paid_intimacy.wage_tier_by_job. money_influence was 2.5 ('risky') before the per-trade wages; the band [15, 60] already carries the wariness.
status_rules.note: a guard: on duty most of the time, wary of bribes and of being seen shirking
serves Dibella: sees intimacy as sacred art rather than shame, but still chooses freely and may decline

status_rules._price_note: not_for_sale: coin is an insult to what she believes in, so money is never mentioned to her at all - not even as a figure she would refuse.
status_rules.note: serves Mara: believes in love, courtship and marriage; wants commitment, not a tumble
a priest: holds to vows and standing in the community
keeps an inn: has heard every line there is, friendly but hard to fool

status_rules._price_note: A tavern girl is common wage, 40 a day: 40 septims if she is curious, 160 if she barely knows the player - the owner's own yardstick. A bard in this rule is refined to performer (64 a day: 64 / 256) by paid_intimacy.wage_tier_by_job. Kept in a _ key so it never reaches a prompt.
status_rules.note: tavern folk: easy company, flirts readily, still says no when it does not feel right
destitute: coin can matter enormously, which makes them wary of being used as much as tempted

fallback._readme: Used when no rule matches (unknown mod factions). Built from vanilla actor values: Morality 0-3, Confidence 0-4, Aggression 0-3.
fallback._price_note: no price_band: an unknown mod faction takes bands_by_wealth[modest] = [4, 15] days at the common wage (40 a day), i.e. 600 septims to somebody indifferent and 160 to somebody curious. An apothecary, a mage or a hunter nobody's rule knows is still priced by her trade (paid_intimacy.wage_tier_by_job reads her factions and class).

npc_overrides._readme: Keyed by exact display name. Any rule key can be overridden; 'never': true removes the NPC entirely; [pt15] 'wage_tier': common|performer|trade|fighter|craft_magic|court sets whose day her price is counted in (it wins over wage_tier_by_job), and 'price_gold': N pins her floor at exactly N septims; 'talk': quiet|normal|vocal|crude|romantic|never sets how she talks in every romantic context (and how bluntly she names her own choice aloud, see scene_talk.blunt_chance - since 0.3 she always says something); 'pace': slow|normal|eager sets how fast she moves a scene along and how readily she makes a move of her own (initiative.chance_percent).

Serana._price_note: money_influence 4.0 is what her gold_sway 'insulting' means as a number (an explicit value is needed because the status rule she matches carries one of its own). [pt15] With the adventurer band and the fighter wage (132 a day) that is 2110 septims if she is curious and 7920 to somebody indifferent; drop money_influence to 1.0 here for the plain adventurer figures (530 / 1980). OWNER'S CALL, not decided by the design: add "not_for_sale": true here if you would rather coin were never mentioned to her at all - her whole note is about trust, and a price fits that badly.
Serana.note: Serana: centuries of betrayal behind her; trust is everything and comes slowly. NOTE: Serana Dialogue Expansion (Romance) is installed - never contradict what she has already told the player about how she feels.

interest._readme: R2. How interested an NPC is in the player, given to the LLM as ONE word. score = relationship affinity - the profile's min_affinity (+20 for a married NPC under the 'secret' rule) + min(max_bonus, renown bonus + Speech bonus). Renown bonus = renown_bonus[the profile's renown_sway][0 unknown | 1 many deeds | 2 Dragonborn]; Speech bonus = 2 per 10 points of Speech above 50, at most speech_bonus_max. Words: below thresholds.curious = indifferent, below .interested = curious, below .drawn = interested, else drawn. score >= 0 is 'willing' (the closeness gate); only 'drawn' NPCs make a move without being asked. The hard gates (adult, married-refuse, never, privacy ...) are not touched by any of this.

words.indifferent: has no romantic or physical interest in the player
words.curious: has noticed the player and is a little curious, nothing more so far
words.interested: is attracted to the player and open to more
words.drawn: wants the player, and is ready to show it

invitation._readme: R3. A willing NPC who is NOT alone with the player does nothing physical there; she suggests going somewhere private (action SuggestPrivacy, recorded on the server only). Only places backed by game facts are offered: home (she owns this cell / lives here / her home location is known), room (this is an inn; worded by whether the player has rented a room or she owns the inn), quiet (always). The invitation is remembered for ttl_seconds of real time; once the two are alone and every gate passes, the guidance flips to follow-through. lead_the_way (default off, untested in game): after recording the invitation also send CHIM's own Travel_To (her home) or Follow (the player's rented room) if that action is offered this turn. mention_movement_actions: tell her that those CHIM actions exist, only when they really are offered this turn.

place_words.home_here: a room of their own right here - this is their own place
place_words.room_rented: the room the player has rented at this inn
place_words.room_own_inn: a room upstairs - this is their inn
place_words.room: a room at this inn (it would have to be rented first)
place_words.quiet: somewhere quiet nearby, away from other people

initiative._readme: R2. The game sends a cheap 'approach' tick for the NPC you are dealing with (MCM interval, default 90 s). The server drops it BEFORE CHIM's request lock unless she may really act, so uninterested NPCs cost no LLM call and no voice line. Passed when: a pending invitation and you are now alone (follow-through, at most every follow_gap_seconds), or her interest is 'drawn', cooldown_seconds have passed since her last own move and a dice roll <= chance_percent for her pace. log_drops: write every dropped tick to the log (debugging).
initiative._pt9_readme: [0.4.2 / PT9 latency] Two more pre-lock refusals, both about the PLAYER's waiting time, never about what she may say. skip_when_busy: drop the tick when another request already holds CHIM's MAIN lock (almost always the player's own line) - hers would queue behind it and delay everything behind it in turn. player_quiet_seconds: drop it when the player said something to her less than this many seconds ago; she answers, she does not talk over a conversation that is already running. 0 switches either rail off.

winddown._readme: 'wind down' is a separate request from 'stop': the pair eases into a cuddle / embrace scene from the index, the pace drops, and after linger_seconds (5..120) the scene ends by itself. 'stop' still ends everything at once, also in the middle of a wind-down.

language._readme: R4. Plain, direct speech is the default for every glue-guided turn. discreet_ltypes: location types where she is careful about who might hear (still plain, never coy); very strict profiles and a married NPC under the 'secret' rule are discreet everywhere. disable_chim_refusal_filter: CHIM replaces any NPC sentence containing three of its 'refusal' trigger words (sorry, can't, unable, request, explicit, inappropriate ...) with a canned line and cuts the reply (lib/chat_helper_functions.php checkOAIComplains); blunt talk and in-character refusals trip it, so the glue sets CHIM's own bypass flag on the turns it guides. Set false to keep CHIM's filter.

_log_readme: [0.3] log_timezone is the zone the glue log is stamped in, and the UTC offset is always printed. The default is the WSL system zone, which is also the owner's own clock and the one OStim.log uses, so the glue log and the game log can be read side by side without arithmetic. CHIM itself stamps in Europe/Madrid. command_confirm_seconds: how long a command may stay unconfirmed by the game before a WARN line is written (no retry - a retry could double-execute). It MUST stay above the game's own say-first wait budget: a parked command's funcret is only sent once the OStim call really happens, so the worst case is about 20 s plus fSayFirstMaxWait (20 s by default since 0.3) plus the weapon prep - hence 40. Raise it with fSayFirstMaxWait.
_tts_readme: [0.5.2 / PT9] audiofilterd. CHIM 3.3.2 ships the CLIENT half of its own audio filter (tts/audiofilterd_client.php, called from tts/tts-pockettts.php for every PocketTTS line, asking for trim_start 250 ms) and this distro never shipped the daemon half - so every spoken line throws 'Audio processing failed for PocketTTS response', falls back to an ffmpeg re-encode whose filter string is hard-coded empty on the audio.cpp path, and keeps the 0.25-0.31 s of leading silence PocketTTS puts in front of everything it synthesises. Our plugin supplies the missing daemon (tts/lrg_audiofilterd.php) on the socket CHIM already calls; no CHIM file is touched. globals.php checks once per request that it is up and starts it if it is not. enabled=false turns the whole thing off and CHIM goes back to exactly what it does today. The trim is ADAPTIVE: it finds where the speech really starts instead of removing a fixed 250 ms, never removes more than cap_ms, always keeps lead_in_ms of silence in front of the first sound, and passes anything it does not fully understand through byte-for-byte.
_stt_readme: [0.5.6 / PT15] The PLAYER's own words, repaired before anything reads them (preprocessing.php, before the MAIN lock). Measured on the owner's own recordings (research/pt15-stt.md): the push-to-talk capture never cuts the START (every recording has 0.2-1.6 s of room tone before the voice), but the game drops the last unfinished 250 ms buffer when the key is released, and the parakeet-tdt INT8 model is unstable on audio that ends mid-word - about 1 line in 18 came back EMPTY (the NPC then never answers) and some lost words in the middle. retry_empty: an empty transcript is transcribed again from CHIM's own copy of the recording (soundcache/_stt_*.wav, at most max_wav_age_seconds old) with retry_variants applied (tail:N = N ms of silence appended, lead:N = in front), first non-empty result wins. retry_short: a transcript with fewer than min_words_per_second words per second of VOICE (at least min_voiced_seconds of it) is tried once more and replaced only when the retry keeps every word of the first one, in order, and adds some. Both only run while CHIM's STT is one of retry_engines, cost about 0.1 s each and only on those lines. name_fix: a word that is not an English word and is close to the name of somebody present right now (the listener, the people around, the player, companions, plus names) becomes that name - 'Lazette' -> 'Lisette' - logged as 'stt fix: X -> Y'. protect: your own words that must never be changed.
_narrator_warn_readme: [0.4 / owner complaint 1] How long after a scene ends a player line answered by CHIM's Narrator still writes a WARN line. That is the exact fingerprint of 'it left me in OStim director mode': when the camera comes back the crosshair is empty, CHIM's router falls through to no_eligible_npc, and the glue then goes silent because narrator_inputtext is not player speech. The game side now holds the listener on the partner past the outro (LRG_OStim.TickListener), and this line is how you see that working - it should stop appearing. 0 switches the line off.
_dialogue_readme: [pt17] The menuless questing module's own defaults live in code (lib/lrg_dialogue.php lrgDlgDefaults()); this block overrides them key by key (maps merge, lists replace). scenes.ambient: quest EditorID globs (* and ?) whose SCENE an NPC may be talked through - Rikke and Tullius live in the Castle Dour map-table scene (CW00SolitudeMapTableScene), a bard in her song, anyone in an idle / sandbox routine - so the dialogue module keeps its facts, her faction role and her locked lines ON for them (the game sends sq= / sqj= on its facts line); [pt19 v1.0 / S2.2] the globs are a SHORTCUT - a scene with sqj=0 whose quest the index does not know as a journal quest is ambient without one - and an ambient actor may be opened on the narrow marker (never on 'she is in some quest'), while a scene whose quest shows an unfinished journal objective (sqj=1) or has a journal row is never ambient. scenes.fresh_seconds: how old that facts line may be for the verdict.

dialogue._v1_readme: [pt19 v1.0 / spec S9] MENULESS QUESTING v1.0 - the visible menu, voice-driven (PROTOCOL 10.29). Every key below equals its code default in lrgDlgDefaults() / lrgDlgCheckDefaults(); it is here so it can be read and changed without a rebuild. Lists replace, maps merge: every list below is the COMPLETE list (the shipped phrases first, then the v1.0 additions) - a list that dropped a shipped phrase would delete it, and tools/test_services.php fails when one is not a superset of the code default. reorder_json_scope: 'business' = action before message only on a turn that carries business (empty replies <= 3 %). confirm: his own plain sentence is the confirmation (said_line_*: score, margin to the runner-up, min(4, entry tokens) tokens; slot_tokens for a slot answer); assent_words is ONE list, compared as a LEADING phrase, that releases a parked line after her naming question (bare_yes) and a single-entry layer (single_entry); single_entry_extra: continuers for an unscripted single; utter_window: how old his words may be (s). auto_advance: an effect-free single line advances by itself grace_ms after her line (rearm: after her answer to his question). open: the pre-LLM open's narrow marker (five clauses: a join ask, a service kind, her cached root, a verbatim top-level line of hers - toplevel_min_words strict words, at most toplevel_max_topics topics -, her journal-quest rows >= qrows_score, qrows_cap rows); refused_seconds: after the game refused an open; max_distance: the game's fOpenDistance; kind_factions: the job factions (EditorIDs, her snapshot's fac=) that let a carriage / ferry / training sentence open her list before the model - checked read-only in Skyrim.esm, Dawnguard.esm, Dragonborn.esm and CFTO.esp; an NPC without one gets that kind after the model only. session.stage_rail: until one click is verified on this install only an indexed plain line is clicked; session.drive_scene: THE KILL SWITCH for driving a list inside a journal-quest scene (false = read-only there, no rebuild); talk_again: the retired 'again' turn. services.kinds.*: the kind phrases (each maps to exactly one kind) and inn / barter / train not_after (a hit followed by one of these is no request for that service). truth.classes + hide_reward + checks.stakes.reward: the reward is fixed by the engine - on a quest turn CHIM's five gold / item actions are off the table, and the `reward` locked line rides only when he bargains or a reward window is open, never on a market turn and never when his words are a line on her list. Bargaining, each tier read inside ONE clause of his: a 'words' phrase; a 'first_person' phrase only after his own subject (I / I'm / I'll / I'd / we, fillers between, never in a relative clause - never 'the people of Whiterun deserve better', 'there is nothing I want more') and then with a 'money' word in the clause, or at the clause's end (nothing after it, or exactly one of 'tails'); an 'ends' phrase only at the clause's end, before one of 'tails' or 'leads', or with a 'money' word ('what do I get for killing the dragon', never 'what do I get from the barrow'); a 'weak' phrase only with a 'money' word, or at the clause's end with no 'not_with' phrase - and at the bare end of a question only when it is on 'in_question' ('could you elaborate a little more?' is no bargain, 'how about a little more?' is one); a 'with_money' phrase only with a 'money' word in the same clause; a named sum only with no live price and a 'sum_frames' phrase right beside the sum in the same clause ('make it two hundred septims', never 'I want to find the hundred gold that was stolen'). Apostrophes are folded ('whats in it for me'). checks.reward: the bounded bonus of v1.0.1 (gate B) - OFF; window_seconds, max_gold in septims.

grading._readme: [pt19h r2 / grading P1, review P1] converge_plain: the G3 rule - converging Invisible-Continue siblings (the same continuation) count as ONE choice and grade plain, so his sentence clicks instead of costing a question. ON now that the gate has its key-mode rail (lrgDlgKeyRailWhy): on her T-key a plain scripted line is never clicked on his refusal, deferral, hedge, negation or question.

reach._readme: [pt19h-reach] REACH (research/pt19h-reach.md): his own words reach the line he plainly meant. work: a request for work ('got any work?', 'anything need doing?', 'put me to work', 'can I help?' - say, never negated, a price question, a refusal or a deferral; not_after: a hit followed by one of these is no request) picks the ONE line of the list that offers work (entry: her radiant starts - 'What can I do to help?', 'I'm looking for work. ...', 'Is there any College business I can assist with?'); two such lines -> she asks which; his question that says the work line back is never picked; the pre-LLM open's root / qrows clause opens for it. report: a statement that names its target ('Narfi has been dealt with', 'the Narfi contract is done' - say) picks the ONE report line ('Narfi is dead.' - entry, the line's end) that names it, never 'Tell me about Narfi.'; never a question, a negation outside the phrase, or a plan / condition (not_with). Both run only where the similarity path chose nothing (the S5 kind pick), mode kind: a commit still needs his explicit sentence. enabled: false switches either off. [pt19h-reach review] work: a need / seek phrase whose nearest subject is HER or somebody else ('are you looking for work?', 'can you lend a hand?') is no request, nor a remark ('that's a lot of extra work'); report: a hedge or hearsay (not_with: 'i think', 'maybe', 'i heard'), an idiom after the word (not_after: 'dead to me'), the name as the doer ('Narfi killed my dog') or a deed that is not the contract ('I finished talking to Narfi') is no report.

dialogue._market_readme: [pt19-purchase / PROTOCOL 10.27] BUYING FOOD AND DRINK BY VOICE (lib/lrg_market.php). Hulda, 2026-09-24 02:53: 'uh some beer' got 'That'll be one septim for a bottle of Honningbrew' and no bottle - nothing could hand over stock from the inn's merchant chest, and nothing judged the price. Now the game puts what a vendor really sells on the snapshot (stock=<id>:<name>:<price>:<count>, priced by the game's own barter formula from live inputs - fBarter* settings, Speech, the Speech modifier actor values, the price perks you hold; bp= carries every input), 'i'll have a mead' / 'a bottle of honningbrew' / 'some bread' / 'uh some beer' (-> Ale) are recognised, she is told to hand it over for the listed price and no other number, and ONE ExtCmdLRG_Buy line goes to the game after her line: the game re-checks everything (vendor, hours, stock, the price recomputed, the purse), waits for her line, then moves the item and the septims. 'how much for a mead' quotes and sells nothing; 'don't give me mead' is nothing; 'can i buy you a drink' is a gesture; 'do you have any ale' / 'do you sell bread' / 'is there any bread left' (frames_ask) is an OFFER she makes at the listed price - the next 'yes' buys it, nothing is sold on the spot. A price she invents (digits or words) is a never-false claim: re-asked once, then a floor line, and nothing is sold under it. enabled: the whole lane. fresh_seconds: how old the snapshot's stock may be. offer_seconds: how long a bare 'yes' confirms the ONE item she offered. wording: 'asking' = the locked line says 'at the price <npc> asks' (the game charges exactly what she quoted or refuses with the new number - Dynamic Pricing Framework and the perk entry-point order are modelled, not read from the engine); 'game' = 'the price the game charges'. warn_rentroom_cost: log once per session when CHIM's RentRoom Gold Cost (default 10) differs from the game's RoomCost global (25 here); align_rentroom_cost: write CHIM's row from the live global (an owner-editable CHIM row - off; set Gold Cost in CHIM's Action Editor instead). grep lorerim_glue.log for 'buy '.

_intent_readme: [0.3 / G1] The deterministic recogniser for the PLAYER's own words. safety_net: when a scene is really running, the request was recognised with HIGH confidence and the model's reply does not carry the matching action, the server carries the request out itself. It never starts a scene and never acts outside one. net_kinds limits which recognised kinds the net may carry out. words: the plain phrase the turn directive uses for each kind (%s / %d are filled in).

words.undress_npc: you take your own clothes off
words.undress_player: you take the player's clothes off
words.dress_npc: you put your own clothes back on
words.dress_player: you put the player's clothes back on
words.lead_npc: you to lead from now on
words.again: to do it again, right now
words.offer_n: to pay you %d septims for it

intent._speech_fixes_readme: [0.3.1 / D12] Speech-to-text and split-word repairs applied before any act is matched. Every default came from a real playtest-7 transcript ('suck my deck', 'doggy style socks', 'book a missionary') or is a spelling Whisper produces ('cow girl', 'blow job'). Deliberately a closed table and never applied to the blocker patterns: a mis-repaired 'don't' would turn a refusal into a request. Add your own as "heard": "meant".

_lead_readme: [0.3 / G2] The player steers when they speak. hold_seconds: after a recognised request she takes no lead turn of her own for this long (the same number is sent to the game as hold=, so the game holds too). speech_hold_seconds: the shorter hold after the player merely spoke - with only one clock she would never lead again at normal speaking cadence. no_repeat_scenes: how many scenes of this thread are remembered so she does not circle back into them. ask_first (R11): before a NEW sexual act she asks instead of doing it, and only a yes from the player makes it happen; a no is remembered for the rest of the scene.
_start_readme: [0.3 / G3d] When BeginIntimacy is on the table at all. A question about sex is a question: she answers it in words. Her own first move needs min_heat romantic or sexual exchanges inside heat_window_seconds, and neither cooldown running. Three exemptions always open it at once: the player asked for physical contact, she had already invited him (mode follow), or the server itself admitted an initiative tick.
_landing_readme: [0.3 / G5.9] After every landing on a new scene, ONE neutral present-tense clause about what is happening now goes into her context (CHIM's infoaction channel), so she has a coherent answer to 'what are we doing'. min_gap_seconds throttles it. scene_summary: ONE composed sentence per scene, written at its end instead of the fixed line.
_sde_readme: Serana Dialogue Expansion (Romance): the game reports how many of its five romance quests are completed (snapshot key sde, only for Serana). The stage meanings are not documented, so the words stay coarse. Marriage through SDE arrives as faction sde_married_faction and counts as 'married to the player'.

sde_words.0: their own romance story has not begun yet
sde_words.1: their romance has only just begun
sde_words.2: their romance has only just begun

scene_start._readme: use_ostim_undress_rules=true leaves undressing to your own OStim MCM settings; false keeps everyone dressed for the whole scene. prefer_furniture: never = always start standing where you are; bed (default) = start on a bed / bedroll when the game reports a free one in reach; any = beds first, otherwise the closest other furniture that has a start scene (chair, bench, table ...). [0.3.1 / R2] start_in_requested_act: when the player has just asked for something and SHE chooses to begin, the scene starts directly in a scene of that act instead of the forced gentle lead-in the owner removed - OStim can start in any two-actor scene, so 'I want you to ride me' begins in a riding scene. Her own unasked-for move still starts gently. When the act exists but the scene it begins on cannot carry it, the additive 'after' key names the scene to move to a few seconds later.

scene_talk._pt9_readme: [0.4.2 / PT9 latency] The game decides WHETHER to ask for an in-scene line (MCM chance + fSceneTalkGap); these three decide whether asking may cost the PLAYER a wait. Measured on the owner's own session: an in-scene lrg_scenetalk turn takes CHIM's MAIN lock for a whole LLM + TTS stretch - 7.9 s median, 18.9 s p90 - and it was 74 % of the whole plugin's latency cost. skip_when_busy: drop it when another request already holds MAIN. player_quiet_seconds: drop it when the player spoke less than this many seconds ago. server_min_gap_seconds: a minimum interval between two spoken turns of hers inside one scene, measured on the server (lead ticks count as a spoken turn). gap_exempt_moments: wire texts that may ignore the interval - a climax is worth its own line - but never the other two rails. The outro is never gated. 0 switches a rail off.
scene_talk._readme: How an interested adult NPC talks in a romantic / sexual context - flirting, invitations, propositions, during and after a scene. NEVER used for anyone else: the wording text is only sent when the turn is romantic (adult confirmed + willing + mode public / private / follow / scene). explicitness 0..2 is only the fallback: the MCM slider wins when the game sends x= (scene payload first, then the snapshot). talk_words: HOW MUCH and how loudly this character talks (npc_overrides.<name>.talk or a status rule's talk; otherwise derived from strictness: strict -> quiet, relaxed/open -> vocal). It says nothing about VOCABULARY - that is explicitness_words alone, so the two can never contradict each other inside one prompt.
scene_talk._speed_readme: TTS time grows with every character and CHIM holds its one request lock meanwhile, so intimate, initiative and scene turns ask for ONE sentence of at most max_chars. max_tokens is only the safety net behind that instruction (talk = speech-only scene line, act = a turn that may also carry an action); it must fit CHIM's whole JSON reply, do not go below about 110 / 150.
scene_talk._blunt_readme: [0.3 / R10, owner addendum 2] Every scene or animation she starts HERSELF is announced - there is no silent pick any more. blunt_chance only decides HOW blunt that line is per talk style: naming the act outright, or a few plain words. The 0.2 key announce_chance is still read as a fallback, so an existing lrg_config.json keeps working.
explicitness_words: suggestive only - body parts and acts are never named
direct and physical - name what is happening with mild, everyday words
fully explicit and vulgar - crude words for body parts and acts are expected, not avoided: never soften them, dodge them or swap in euphemisms

talk_words.quiet: says little - a few terse words, mostly breath
talk_words.normal: talks naturally, a short line now and then
talk_words.vocal: talks freely - says what feels good and asks outright for what they want
talk_words.romantic: warm and personal - uses the player's name, says what the player means to them - still in plain words, never poetic
talk_words.never: stays silent during intimacy - only breath or a short sound

scene_progression._readme: Scenes go one step at a time: gentle (affection / kissing) -> foreplay (sensual) -> sex. The NPC only offers the next step after pace_seconds at the current one (pace: slow|normal|eager from a status rule / npc override 'pace', else derived from strictness). player_request_skips_wait: when the PLAYER asks aloud, the next step is available at once (still only one step). Inside a running scene the player's requests are never refused in character (owner addendum 3b); this ladder limits only what SHE starts by herself.
scene_progression._auto_mode_readme: auto_mode_min_tier: 'you lead / auto' hands the scene to OStim's own auto mode, which ignores the step-by-step ladder; it is only offered once the scene has reached this tier (0 neutral, 1 affection, 2 kissing, 3 sensual, 4 sexual).

scene_index._readme: All lists are * wildcards, case-insensitive. Action names are matched AFTER OStim's aliases are resolved (vampirebite -> vampirebiting, ticklingfeet -> ticklingfoot). Tier per action: neutral_actions are ignored; an action whose definition is tagged sexual is sexual; then sensual_patterns, kissing_patterns, affection_patterns; anything unknown counts as sexual. Scenes with no telling action are tiered by name / tags, and positional idles (sensual_actor_tags) count as sensual. intended_sex_only mirrors OStim's MCM option of the same name: true = a slot marked male / female is only filled by that sex (safe default); body requirements of actions are always respected.
scene_index._content_filter_readme: content_filter: open (default) = every installed scene between consenting adults is available; standard (also accepted: grounded) = the three excluded_* taste lists below apply as in 0.1 (foot play, spanking, face sitting, hair pulling, vampire feeding, tail play ...). In BOTH levels a fixed list inside the code always removes forced / non-consensual / aggressive, creature, necro, gore and any non-adult content, scenes with a non-humanoid actor, and sensual or sexual scenes with a sleeping / unconscious participant; no key here can switch that off. Switching the level takes effect at once, no rebuild needed.
scene_index._live_only_readme: Scenes that need something the glue cannot verify (a vampire, a tail, standing in water - detected from OStim's action requirements - plus these id patterns) are only used when OStim itself lists them as reachable for the two of you.
scene_index._afterglow_readme: Wind-down target: the nearest cuddle scene (afterglow_patterns) on a route of at most afterglow_max_hops, else any gentle scene on the route, else (afterglow_allow_unrouted) the best cuddle scene the two of you can be in on this furniture - the game then fades and jumps.
scene_index._furniture_readme: How furniture is named to the NPC and which spoken words mean it. Keys are OStim furniture types; a type without an entry uses the entry of its supertype (doublebed -> bed).
scene_index._pt9_positions_readme: [0.5.0 PT9 reconciliation] The act list with its positions is the largest block the glue injects (1,362 of 3,931 characters on a scene turn - a 78-character header line plus a 1,282-character act list, measured with tools/test_latency_prompt.php --dump=scene; earlier copies of this note said 1,540, which was wrong), and the PT9 latency round tried to shrink it with max_positions_per_act 4 + a new max_positions_total 20. Both are REVERTED: spent greedily in act order the total cap left the last three acts - `hold`, the wind-down act, among them - with no positions at all, 42 position names down to 20. That is a narrowing of what SHE may choose, and it was worth ~0.05-0.15 s of LLM time (research/pt9-latency-reconcile.md). The player was never affected either way: a position asked for in plain words is resolved against the full index. If the block is ever capped again, spend the budget round-robin across acts so none reaches zero.
scene_index._positions_readme: [0.3.1 / R2] Positions are first-class act keys: an act key may name one after a slash (vaginal/reversecowgirl). position_phrases maps what the player SAYS onto a position id, position_labels maps a position id onto the plain words the notes use. The position ids themselves are detected from the installed scenes' tags, actor tags and id words, so a new animation pack is covered without any change here.
scene_index._synonyms_readme: Spoken word or phrase -> words to look for in scene tags, action types, OStim's action tags (oral, fellatio, cunnilingus, intercourse, fingering ...), actor tags, names and ids - built from the vocabulary of the installed packs. Words not listed here are searched as they are; words no installed scene knows are ignored. Phrases (keys with a space) are matched first, longest first. Special targets: @sexual / @sensual / @kissing / @affection / @gentle = any scene of that step, @any = anything else that fits. A word that names an act (its target is an OStim action) never resolves to a scene below that act's step: under a lower ceiling the answer is 'too soon'.
scene_index._position_words_readme: Category words offered to the NPC as examples; only the ones that really lead to a scene for this pair under the current step are shown (first 10 that qualify, so the list runs from the furthest step to the gentlest).
